memo.verdict: Neutral at 30.96 EUR (2026-09-24); bullish at or below 30 EUR, the price at which the modal path clears 20% a year over eighteen months (29.8 EUR at 16.0x; 30.2 EUR at the blended 16.2x; 27.4 EUR on the three-year test). Progress to Early-Stage rather than park. Conviction: medium on the business and the demand; a working hypothesis on the return, because the return leg rests on the interest line and the sector's multiple, neither of which the company controls. The park rule does not bite: no D or F on management ('No mediocre management' B), business quality ('Business' B), predictability ('Transmission' B) or trackability ('Leading indicators' C). Triggers named: a book-to-bill below 1.0x at the 9 November 2026 trading update or at FY2026, or the 902 EURm of options not exercised through the Q4 2026 season; a reported half-year adjusted EBIT margin below 26% (Invalidate); gross margin below 33% (Alarm); net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x at late 2027 with no asset sale under way (Invalidate), or at or above 3.5x, the covenant (Invalidate); a new acquisition before HGH is integrated (Alarm); tube lead times above 20 months, Harder below 15,000 tubes, net working capital above 43% of revenue, Kappa below 35 EURm in FY2026 (Alarms).
case: - The thesis: Theon is a contracted demand-inflection case in European soldier optronics, compelling at the operating line and only adequate at the shareholder's line at 30.96 EUR. The company has turned a policy-backed rearmament cycle into a 1.46 EURbn backlog and a 26.2% margin, but financed its expansion with 8.6m new shares and about 550 EURm of peak net debt, so EBITDA growing at about 30% a year reaches EPS at about 20%, and the modal return is about 17% a year over eighteen months and 15% over three years against the 20% bar. At about 30 EUR, 3% below the price, the modal path clears the bar.

- The external force is sector-wide, structural and contracted. European order intake across Morgan Stanley's coverage +25% to over 85 EURbn, aggregate backlog a record 438 EURbn (September 2026); NATO 5% of GDP by 2035 with 3.5% core; Germany 180 EURbn by 2030; SAFE 150 EURbn; militaries moving to one-to-one soldier equipping. Theon's 1 EURbn OCCAR framework (100,000 devices for Germany, 4,000 for Belgium, December 2025) is the largest night-vision procurement in NATO history. Direction by force: demand tailwind intensifying; core competition mild tailwind (the US primes ITAR-blocked, the European primes avoid Theon's markets), headwind at the platform and upstream edges; regulation tailwind (Buy-European 35% non-EU component cap, EU design authority, Omnibus V ten-year frameworks); own cycle turning up (experts' peak 2028 to 2029); macro neutral except the cost of money; supply side headwind D; the sector multiple a headwind to the price (C).

- The internal change is broad and leverage-funded: guidance raised twice in 2026 (A); balance-sheet utilisation B with the 'dangerous leverage' flag partly present (0.4x to 0.5x of covenant headroom); strategy pivot to 50/50 by 2029 resourced (B, empire-building flag plausible, five transactions in twelve months); acquisitions coherent and delivering (Kappa 11 points of H1 growth, a 42 EURm order) but discipline unproven at HGH's price (B); new products A (PHYLAX over 40 EURm, Kappa 42 EURm plus 27 EURm options, 100 EURm thermal clip-on, 70 EURm IdZ, record 25 EURm Harder third-party order); new geographies B (Europe still 83.1% of backlog); standards B; shareholder returns D (payout cut to 20% to 30%, rights issue at 30% discount); the Exosens reversal C; price rises C (industry prices up 2.5x to 3.0x since 2022 but passed through back-to-back, OCCAR "priced competitively"); no chief-executive change (D, an absence); perimeter widening (F, an absence).
counter_case: - At the whole-case level: Theon is a cyclical peak bought with leverage. European soldier-equipment demand is a two-to-three-year replenishment surge that peaks in 2027 to 2029, as the company's own former managers say; the largest contract is an agency framework priced for volume, and agency buying rises to 40% of European procurement by 2030, so the 26% margin is a pre-OCCAR artefact that compresses to the 15% to 18% the experts expect as volumes roll off; the founder has spent the peak's cash and about 550 EURm of debt on a supplier's minority stake with no control, a French acquisition at 18.5x EBITDA and a scatter of platform and AI ventures where Theon has no proven edge; free cash flow on FactSet's definition was 16.9% of net income in FY2025 and working capital eats 41 cents of every revenue euro; the balance sheet reaches 3.0x to 3.1x against a 3.5x covenant in the very quarter a ceasefire could delay the tranches; and the precedent for the fix is a rights issue at a 30% discount. On that reading the stock de-rates from 16.4x on peak earnings to the crash band of 10.1x on falling ones, 19.1 EUR or lower, and Deutsche Bank's free-cash-flow-yield value of 18.00 EUR is the honest number. The sector has already de-rated 20% to 38% over twelve months.

- Conceded: the timing of the leverage is poor and self-inflicted; the free-cash-flow record on any definition but the company's is weak; the Exosens stake is a governance oddity we would not have made; the R&D budget (2.8% of revenue) does not support the software ambition; the drop-through sensitivity shows the modal return falling to a D on a modest adverse ratio.
triggers: - Backlog conversion: a book-to-bill below 1.0x at the 9 November 2026 update or at FY2026, or the 902 EURm of options not exercised through the Q4 2026 season, would change the view; the record puts conversion at about 75%.

- Margin: a reported half-year adjusted EBIT margin below 26% invalidates; gross margin below 33% is the alarm; the record puts the margin holding at about 70%; the experts' 15% to 18% at the cycle's peak is the skew.

- Deleveraging: net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x at late 2027 (the H1 2027 report in September 2027 is the named check) with no asset sale under way invalidates; at or above 3.5x, the covenant, invalidates at any time; a new acquisition before HGH is integrated is the alarm; the record puts deleveraging at about 65%.

- The multiple: no sector de-rating inside eighteen months is put at 55%, so a de-rating is plausible; the re-rating needs both a cleaner balance sheet and a sector that stops falling, and neither is given better than two-to-one.
- Tube supply: lead times above 20 months or Harder below 15,000 tubes are the alarms; the record puts supply holding to 2030 at about 80%.
- Other alarms: net working capital above 43% of revenue; Kappa revenue below 35 EURm in FY2026.

judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** Theon is in Defence. Defence's Industry RS was 13 at the Friday 23 October reading (20 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** Theon is in Defence, non-primes. That sector's Sector RS was 13 at the 30 September month-end (52 at the August month-end); on Friday's daily reading it was 10
  - Theon's sector's other companies, with their daily Stock RS: Kongsberg Gruppen (42), Hensoldt (40), Melrose Industries (13), Exosens (51), Exail Technologies (73), Montana Aerospace (13), and 4 more
- **Cohort:** Theon is in Defence electronics, optronics and communications. The cohort's relative strength was 44 on Friday's daily reading (60 four weeks earlier). Theon's cohort's other companies: Hensoldt (40), Exosens (51), Exail Technologies (73), MilDef (87), Ovzon (9)
- **Theon's charts are on Theon's page on the PMS Per-stock Dashboard:** https://vfhqi.github.io/ratings/pms/holding.html?t=THEON-NL

**What is going on, and why it matters**
- **The price move, by beta:** over twenty sessions Theon's shares fell about 5%; Theon's beta of 0.79 explains almost none of it, so Theon's own move was about -5%, half its usual size
- **The industry:** Defence is one of the market's weakest industries (Industry RS 13), and Theon's sector's companies fell about 4% over the same five and twenty sessions, so Theon is moving with its group
- **The analysts:** for Theon, Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates was +22% and Net Upgrade Breadth, target prices -11% at the 30 September month-end, so analysts still raise Theon's sales but cut what they will pay for them

**What it means for the position**
- **Holding:** only your one-off in/out link holds Theon; Theon meets five of the six Sell Criteria, every one except the 30% tranche rule
- **Selling:** ***I recommend selling Theon at Tuesday's session without waiting for a purchase (decision 2 in section 7).*** Separately, Theon is about 7% above the 30% level of both tranches (about EUR 26.82), so a tranche sale under the 30% tranche rule is plausible within weeks if Defence falls again
- **Adding:** adding to Theon is not allowed, because Theon meets a Sell Criterion
- **Theon's place in the order of sale:** first, because Theon meets the most Sell Criteria and has the weakest Stock RS in the book (19 at the 30 September month-end, 22 on Friday's daily reading)
  - Theon would move down only if Defence's relative strength recovered; waiting keeps 4.05% of the fund's capital in the holding the rule most wants gone

**What we could lose:** about 0.28% of the fund's capital, if Theon's price falls to its 30% level at about EUR 26.82

**Experiment: which stocks Theon's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)
- **Exosens** (same sector and cohort): 0.63 and 0.55, strong
- **Kongsberg Gruppen** (same sector): 0.47 and 0.42, moderate
- **Hensoldt** (same sector and cohort): 0.41 and 0.46, moderate
- **MilDef** (same sector and cohort): 0.34 and 0.39, moderate
- **My reading:** look at Exosens first; Theon trades with European defence electronics, so Theon's moves are mostly the group's

**The Investment Analyst's memo on Theon (1 October, at EUR 30.96; digest of 25 September)**
- **Decided:** the memo on Theon progresses the case; it is neutral at EUR 30.96 and bullish at or below EUR 30
- **Must happen:** a book-to-bill of 1.0 or more at the 9 November trading update, the EUR 902 million of options exercised, and a half-year margin of 26% or more
- **Main risk:** a cyclical peak bought with leverage, with agency buying compressing Theon's margin
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** clears our bar of 20% a year at or below about EUR 30; Friday's EUR 28.82 is about 4% below that line
- **Next test:** Theon's trading update on 9 November

**My judgement:** bearish on the Theon position (sell first), medium conviction, lower than a week ago
- The six Sell Criteria sell relative-strength breakdowns whatever the valuation says, Theon's breakdown is the deepest in the book, and Defence is still falling
- **Counter-case, and it is stronger this week:** at EUR 28.82 Theon is now below the memo's bullish line of EUR 30, so the memo would buy what the rule sells; the memo also says that return rests on the Defence sector's multiple, which the market is still marking down

**What would change my view:** Theon's Stock RS above 50 at the 30 October month-end; a book-to-bill above 1.0 on 9 November with Defence turning

items.criterion: MA SLs: each tranche's MA less 2%, information only for a Middle Innings Core Investment

bullets.text: Theon is a Middle Innings Core Investment, so its MA SLs sell nothing; its six Sell Criteria decide the sale.
Theon's MA SL exits were confirmed for both tranches on 28-Sep, on a €29.24 close 5.5% below the 200D MA SL stop.
Theon's SP rose 10.3% from the 8-Oct low to €30.02 on 27-Oct, 3.0% below the MA SL stop, then fell to €28.64 on 28-Oct.

items.criterion: Industry RS below 30, read each Friday

bullets.text: Theon's Industry RS (Defence) was 13 on 27-Oct, a sell signal at every Friday reading since 4-Sep, eight in a row.
Theon's Industry RS sell signal ends if Defence rises about three places among the 16 industries at a Friday reading, as Defence did from 31-Jul to 7-Aug.
Until Theon's Industry RS sell signal ends, the rules sell the whole Theon holding when its replacement is bought; Theon is first in my proposed order of sale.

items.criterion: The 200D MA of relative price flat or falling over the month, read each Friday

bullets.text: Theon's relative 200D MA was falling, a sell signal, every Friday since 2-Oct, and fell (1.09%) over the month to 27-Oct.
Theon's relative 200D MA will still be falling on Fri 30-Oct, and Theon's relative price must rise about 9% to stop that fall by the 6 and 13-Nov readings.
Theon's relative 200D MA sell signal keeps the whole Theon holding for sale, whatever Theon's relative price against its 52W high reads.

items.criterion: Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70, read at the month-end

bullets.text: Theon's Sector RS test has been a sell signal since the 30-Sep month-end, with Theon's Sector RS at 13 and Stock RS at 27 on 27-Oct.
Theon's Sector RS sell signal very probably stays at the Fri 30-Oct month-end, as ending it needs Theon's Sector RS at 50 or Stock RS at 70.
Theon's Sector RS sell signal keeps Theon in the order of sale under your one-off in/out link.

bullets.text: Theon's Stock RS with Net Upgrade Breadth test has been a sell signal since the 30-Sep month-end, firmer on 27-Oct with Stock RS 27 and PT Net Upgrade Breadth (25%).
Theon's Stock RS sell signal very probably stays at the Fri 30-Oct month-end, as ending it needs Theon's Stock RS at 50 or two PT raises without further cuts.
Theon's PT changes after Theon's 9-Nov third-quarter trading update will set Theon's PT Net Upgrade Breadth.

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

Theon's room of 2.63% is more than one tranche of 1.67%, and the 6.68% limit stops adds but never forces a sale.
A full 1.67% tranche would take Theon to 5.72% of capital, leaving 0.96% of room, less than a further full tranche.

A rise in Theon's Stock RS, with EPS estimates turning up alongside the rising revenue estimates, would turn the technicals and sell-side towards a broadening case.

Your 22-Sep note asked whether Theon's pullback "from end of August at 37 EUR down to 32 EUR" was "a positive retest"; Theon's 200D MA SL exit on 28-Sep answered no.
A new position note from you on Theon would set the tag.
